examples.japanese: {工事|こうじ}{現場|げんば}では{安全靴|あんぜんぐつ}が{必須|ひっす}だ。
examples.english: Safety shoes are required at construction sites.

examples.japanese: {安全靴|あんぜんぐつ}を{履|は}いていたおかげで{怪我|けが}をせずに{済|す}んだ。
examples.english: I was spared from injury thanks to wearing safety shoes.

examples.japanese: {新入|しんにゅう}{社員|しゃいん}には{会社|かいしゃ}から{安全靴|あんぜんぐつ}とヘルメットが{支給|しきゅう}される。
examples.english: New employees are provided with safety shoes and helmets by the company.

notes:
Footwear with reinforced toes (usually steel or composite) designed to protect workers from falling objects, crushing, and other workplace hazards. Required in many industrial and construction settings in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {安全靴|あんぜんぐつ}を{履|は}く: to wear safety shoes
- {安全靴|あんぜんぐつ}の{着用|ちゃくよう}: wearing safety shoes
- {安全靴|あんぜんぐつ}が{必要|ひつよう}: safety shoes are needed

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {長靴|ながぐつ}: rubber boots — waterproof boots, not necessarily reinforced for safety
- {作業靴|さぎょうぐつ}: work shoes — general work footwear without the specific safety reinforcement
- ヘルメット: helmet — another piece of standard safety equipment, protects the head
